controls.reason: Timing and effort can be measured, but deciding how the result should reduce migration bottlenecks requires contextual diagnosis and an effectiveness judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A record can contain exact replacement hours and cost while the chosen change removes an insignificant delay and leaves the true approval bottleneck untouched.

controls.reason: Identifying every quantum-vulnerable use across eleven technical and supplier domains requires a complete, current estate and dependency inventory.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All registered systems can be classified while an embedded device firmware or supplier service uses vulnerable public-key cryptography and is absent.

controls.reason: Migration priority across lifetime, adversary, exposure, criticality, difficulty, interoperability and lead time is a security and business judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every item can receive the seven scores while inappropriate weights place a short-lived low-risk service ahead of a long-lived critical archive.

controls.reason: Roadmap field presence is bounded, but dependency completeness and the adequacy of compatibility, testing, rollback and communication strategies are not.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A roadmap can populate every named field while omitting a legacy relying party and specifying a rollback that re-enables vulnerable cryptography.

controls.reason: The rule does not define representative workloads, measurement protocols, baselines or acceptable impacts for the nine increased resource dimensions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A report can mention all nine dimensions using a tiny fixture while missing certificate-size failure and memory exhaustion under the real workload.

controls.reason: Representative load, failure, interoperability, constrained-device and recovery conditions are contextual, and no exhaustive test oracle is supplied.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The recorded test suite can exercise one case in every category while an actual constrained device fails on a larger hybrid certificate chain.

controls.reason: Preventing weak-only validation and downgrade across every hybrid negotiation path is an adversarial runtime property, not a structured-record fact.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Named downgrade fixtures can pass while a retry through a legacy proxy accepts success after validating only the classical component.

controls.reason: Format version fields do not prove that classical, hybrid and post-quantum material cannot be confused across all parsers and protocol contexts.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All objects can carry distinct version tags while one decoder ignores the tag and interprets hybrid bytes as a valid classical key.

controls.reason: Applicability to long-lived data and devices requires complete discovery, while the adequacy of six migration and archival actions needs specialist judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The plan can cover all known long-lived stores while an unregistered archive lacks re-signing and a dormant device has no firmware update path.

controls.reason: Future ability to replace a post-quantum algorithm after unknown weaknesses or operational limits emerge is an open-ended architectural and runtime claim.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A provider abstraction and replacement plan can pass today while a hard-coded wire format prevents replacing the algorithm on an offline device later.

controls.reason: Including all post-quantum dependencies and migration status in every relevant supplier assurance and procurement decision needs complete supplier and decision inventories.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Current procurement templates can have both fields while an indirect cryptographic provider is omitted from assurance and a renewal decision.

controls.reason: Triggering review after every relevant standard, cryptanalytic development, provider commitment, regulatory deadline or architecture change depends on incomplete external feeds and legal interpretation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every configured trigger can produce a review while a newly applicable regulator deadline or supplier commitment is never ingested.

controls.reason: Ten fields can validate recorded rows, but the register itself cannot prove inclusion of every actual key, certificate, secret, token and trust anchor.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All rows can be complete while an emergency signing key or embedded trust anchor exists outside the authoritative-looking inventory.

controls.reason: Separating eight key purposes across all runtime uses depends on a complete key and call-path inventory rather than declared purpose labels alone.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Inventory rows can assign distinct purposes while an authentication key is reused for webhook signing through an undocumented code path.

controls.reason: Least privilege and separation of duties require contextual role-risk judgment plus complete coverage of eight key-management authorization paths.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The role matrix can look separated while an emergency principal can both generate and activate a production key through an unrecorded interface.

controls.reason: Absence of secrets and private keys across nine broad repositories and outputs is an open-world negative claim beyond finite secret-scanner evidence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Configured scans can pass while an encoded private key remains inside a binary client bundle or archived diagnostic attachment.

controls.reason: Unauthorized, unusual, impending, excessive and unexpected conditions require policy judgment, and monitoring all key activity needs complete telemetry coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Six alert rules can exist while an unusual export through an uninstrumented provider is never observed or classified.

controls.reason: A test record cannot prove routine rotation avoids outage or data loss across all consumers, data copies and timing conditions without a complete protocol.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The happy-path drill can pass while a dormant consumer fails after cutover or a delayed replica loses access to encrypted data.

controls.reason: Testing emergency revocation and replacement after suspected compromise lacks a bounded compromise scenario, dependency inventory and success oracle.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A drill can revoke one test certificate successfully while an offline verifier continues trusting the replaced key during a real incident.

controls.reason: Confirming that old material no longer grants access is universal over every replaced credential copy, verifier, cache, session and authorization path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known login routes can reject the old token while an unregistered integration or cached session still accepts it.

controls.reason: Protection against unauthorized modification and rollback of trust-store updates is an adversarial behavior claim across every update and recovery path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Signature and version tests can pass while a recovery utility accepts an older correctly signed root bundle after a crafted failure.

controls.reason: Which key material is required and what counts as broadly accessible require specialist judgment, while recovery spans incomplete backup and access paths.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A backup plan can recover known keys under declared roles while an unknown replica exposes the same material to a broad operations group.

controls.reason: Procedure definition is bounded, but verifying destruction or cryptographic erasure across every replica, cache, device and retained medium is not.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A signed destruction record can cover all inventory rows while an offline snapshot or device cache retains a recoverable key copy.

controls.reason: Whether an offline or alternate recovery path remains resilient for critical trust and signing systems is an empirical availability and compromise-resistance claim.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A documented recovery channel can pass a normal drill while shared identity dependencies make it unusable when the primary system is compromised.

controls.reason: Reconciliation against actual deployed references and removal of all orphaned or unused material requires complete runtime reference and secret-copy discovery.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The register can match known deployment manifests while a dormant job still references an unlisted secret and an apparently orphaned key is actually needed.

controls.reason: An inventory cannot prove complete discovery of all components that process the sixteen broad classes of untrusted formats and executable content.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every registered parser can be listed while a plugin or transitive library processes serialized objects on an undocumented path.

controls.reason: Disabling six feature classes across all parsers requires a complete component inventory, while deciding which format features are unnecessary is contextual.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known parsers can disable entities and macros while an embedded renderer permits network retrieval that was mislabeled necessary.

controls.reason: Adequate validation limits and allowed content are format-specific security choices, and enforcement must cover every path before expensive processing.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A validator can check all ten named fields while unsafe nesting limits allow resource exhaustion or one alternate path decodes before validation.

controls.reason: Resource-limit configuration over eight dimensions does not prove coverage of every untrusted-processing component or that the selected limits are safe.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All registered workers can have CPU and memory limits while an undocumented converter runs without a process limit and can exhaust the host.

controls.reason: Temporary-storage records do not prove non-executability, access control, bounds, monitoring and reliable cleanup across failures and all storage paths.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Configured temp directories can pass while a fallback directory is executable or crash recovery leaves sensitive files indefinitely.

controls.reason: Preventing six filesystem attack families over arbitrary hostile names, archives, links and races requires an exhaustive adversarial model and path oracle.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Standard traversal fixtures can pass while a symlink swap during extraction escapes the sandbox on an untested filesystem timing.

controls.reason: Mandatory validation and transformation can be policy facts, but moderation is judgment-based and quarantine enforcement must cover every publication path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A state machine can quarantine normal uploads while a retry path publishes after scanning but before required human moderation completes.

controls.reason: Quickly has no stated deadline, and whether disablement or alternate processing is safe depends on parser behavior, workload and operational context.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A dependency can be patched within a locally recorded target while the alternate parser silently drops security metadata and is not actually safe.

controls.reason: Fuzzing records cannot prove complete parser and conversion-boundary coverage, and adversarial adequacy lacks a bounded corpus and oracle.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A fuzzer can run with minimized retained crashes while a different serialization boundary or semantic mutation remains untested and exploitable.

controls.reason: Guaranteeing that every crash, timeout, malformed output and partial-processing path cannot publish unsafe content or leak data is an unbounded runtime safety claim.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known failure tests can pass while a process crash after validation but before commit publishes an unscanned partial file containing internal metadata.

controls.reason: Output validation adequacy and coverage depend on every downstream interpreter's semantics and a complete handoff inventory.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All registered renderers can receive validated output while an undocumented template engine interprets a payload as executable markup.

controls.reason: Monitoring parser failures, resource anomalies, suspicious formats, crashes and escape attempts cannot prove complete instrumentation or correct detection.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Five dashboards can exist while a sandbox escape suppresses telemetry or an uninstrumented conversion worker repeatedly crashes.

controls.reason: Monitored, durable and accessible reporting plus backup-channel availability are operational quality claims with no uptime, reachability or loss oracle.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Two documented channels can exist and emit heartbeats while reports are silently dropped during provider failure or inaccessible to some reporters.

controls.reason: RFC 9116 syntax and location are bounded, but where publication is appropriate and which public Internet properties exist require contextual applicability and complete discovery.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known domains can host a valid file while an undocumented public subdomain lacks one, or a reviewer can incorrectly mark the property out of scope.

controls.reason: A structured security.txt record cannot by itself prove contacts, keys, links, languages, acknowledgments, canonical location and expiration are all currently usable and correct.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every field can be populated and unexpired while the reporting mailbox rejects delivery or the published encryption key has been revoked.

controls.reason: The ten named PSIRT stages form a finite procedure set whose definitions, ownership and version bindings can be checked exactly.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A policy with no duplicate-handling or credit procedure fails the exact ten-stage mapping; the check does not claim incidents are handled effectively.

controls.reason: Complete affected-product and dependency tracking is open-world, while data impact and regulatory implications require security, privacy and legal judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every record can contain the eight fields while an indirect customer dependency is omitted and the regulatory impact is wrongly marked none.

controls.reason: Response and remediation times can be measured, but recurrence completeness, reporter experience and disclosure quality require subjective and incomplete outcome evidence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A dashboard can report all five metrics while a narrow satisfaction score masks a confusing disclosure and unrecognized repeat vulnerabilities.

controls.reason: Periodically has no named cadence, and whether synthetic reports are realistic enough to exercise the PSIRT process is contextual.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An annual exercise can use a simple known bug and complete every workflow step while never testing a realistic cross-product coordinated disclosure.

controls.reason: A versioned telemetry policy can define security-relevant event types for each of the twelve finite behavior domains named by the rule.
controls.counterexample_analysis: If export, deletion or administrative behavior lacks an event definition, the exact domain-to-event policy join fails; runtime collection is not inferred.

controls.reason: Where each of nine fields is appropriate requires contextual applicability, and actual logging must cover every relevant event and code path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The event schema can expose all nine fields while an integration path omits tenant and reason data after being incorrectly marked exempt.

controls.reason: Protecting logs from five threat classes across every writer, store, administrator and retention path is an adversarial runtime claim.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Access controls and immutable-storage tests can pass while a recovery account deletes logs or clock rollback corrupts event ordering.

controls.reason: Absence of seven sensitive data classes across all telemetry is unbounded, while unnecessary personal data and sensitive content require contextual classification.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known schemas can exclude passwords and tokens while an exception string leaks a session identifier or free text containing sensitive personal data.

controls.reason: A versioned telemetry-governance record can define retention, access, purpose and deletion for security telemetry and derived risk profiles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A registered telemetry class or risk profile missing any of the four governance definitions fails the exact schema and registry join.

controls.reason: A policy record is not authoritative proof that all investigator access is time-bounded, purpose-bound and audited across identity and data paths.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The approved access broker can enforce all three properties while a direct database role gives investigators standing, unaudited access.

controls.reason: Realistic attacks and benign edges are contextual, while evasion attempts and telemetry failures span a non-exhaustive adversarial test space.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A detection suite can include all four categories yet miss a low-and-slow evasion that suppresses one telemetry source.

controls.reason: Monitoring five pipeline-failure classes cannot prove complete coverage or detect manipulation that also disables or falsifies the monitor.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All five alerts can pass injections while an attacker suppresses both a telemetry shard and its heartbeat through an unmodeled control-plane path.

controls.reason: Every detection-to-response mapping requires complete detection inventory, while actionable containment and customer protection are contextual effectiveness judgments.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All registered detections can link to five record types while a generic runbook cannot contain the incident and gives customers no useful protection.

controls.reason: The eleven named incident classes form a finite playbook catalog whose current procedure references and owners can be checked exactly.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A catalog without ransomware or widespread-vulnerability handling fails the exact eleven-class join; response effectiveness is not asserted.

controls.reason: A versioned incident-governance plan can define the ten finite authority, response, communication, review, support, evidence and escalation areas.
controls.counterexample_analysis: If legal and privacy review or executive escalation is undefined, the exact ten-area plan schema fails without judging the decisions made.

controls.reason: Whether alternate communication, identity, documentation and recovery channels remain usable under compromise requires empirical independence and availability evidence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Four backup channels can be documented and pass normal tests while all share the compromised primary identity provider.

controls.reason: Identifying every released and deployed artifact derived from five compromised input classes requires complete provenance and deployment inventories.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known artifacts can have signed provenance while an emergency build from the compromised runner was deployed outside the release registry.

controls.reason: Required scale has no numerical threshold, and revocation ability across eight object classes depends on complete inventories and live system behavior.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A drill can revoke the configured sample volume while a real incident exceeds service quotas and leaves unregistered integrations or sessions active.

controls.reason: Clean-room or trusted status and adequate testing for severe supply-chain incidents require specialist trust judgment and a defined compromise protocol.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A documented rebuild can pass one drill while depending on a package mirror or identity root compromised in the incident model.
